your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: It's early, I have $1500, and the light blues are cheap with good ROI. P1 has Connecticut, so this blocks them too. Buy it.
P3 has no light blues, so they want Oriental to block P1 or to use in a later trade. It's a useful blocker for me too. If they pay $210 I'm up $110 in cash, which is worth it. Otherwise I'll keep it.

Orange is the top color group because players coming out of jail land on it so often. Buying costs $180, which leaves me $1220. No one else owns any orange yet. Next I want Tennessee from P1 or New York if it comes up.
If they accept, I hold 2 of 3 oranges with NY unowned, and they get light blues, which are a weaker group. Orange is better than light blue, so the $60 is well spent.

Handing P1 2 of 3 oranges is a real cost, so I need a big premium for it. At $160 I'd hold 2 of 3 light blues plus $1380 in cash, and light blues are cheap to build on. If they come back near $130-150 I'll take it. Below that, I keep St. James as an orange blocker.

I hold 2 of 3 light blues, Vermont is unowned, and I have $1380. Priority is buying Vermont if I land on it, or trading for it if someone else gets it. P1 now has 2 of 3 oranges, so I need to keep New York out of their hands: buy it if I land there.

Nobody owns a yellow yet, and buying leaves me $1120. Atlantic is a good start on that group and works as trade bait. My priorities stay the same: get Vermont to finish the light blues, and block New York so P1 can't complete the oranges.

P2 has Boardwalk and $1456, so they would probably win an auction and complete the dark blues. Buying blocks that and gives me strong trade leverage with P2, either for a big cash premium or as a swap toward completing my own groups. I'll have $770 left. Priorities are still Vermont and blocking New York.

Selling Park Place completes P2's dark blues, which is a big strategic cost, so I need a heavy premium. At $700 they'd be left with about $536, which slows their building, and I'd have $1470 to grab Vermont and build. If they come back around $550-600 plus Penn RR, that's acceptable.

At 550 + Penn RR I'm already in my acceptable range. I'm trying for a bit more. If they push back, I'll take anything at 575 or above, and probably 550 too, rather than lose the deal. The cash lets me chase Vermont and build later. I need to watch dark blue rents once they build.

p4 offers $230 cash for VENTNOR_AVENUE. I hold BALTIC_AVENUE, ST_CHARLES_PLACE, and VENTNOR_AVENUE. p1 has no monopoly. p2 holds a dark blue monopoly with two houses each.

Boardwalk and Park Place rent is severe. Boardwalk costs $600. Park Place costs $500. My $649 barely covers one hit. p4 has $1411 cash and can afford the trade.

p4 already owns Atlantic Avenue. If I accept the trade, they would hold Atlantic and Ventnor, needing only Marvin Gardens to complete the yellow monopoly. That is dangerous.

The offer is a loss. Ventnor costs $260 to buy, so $230 is $30 below face value. The claim of a $90 profit is false. I will reject this trade.

The $230 would not complete any set for me. I already have enough cash to cover one dark blue hit. I will reject the trade.

I will not pay p2. I will not sell St. Charles or Ventnor. I will not mortgage until rent forces it.

My next priorities are buying States, Virginia, Marvin, and Mediterranean. I will bid to block p1's orange and p4's light blue if prices stay survivable.

I could counter by asking for Atlantic Avenue. That would give me two yellows and leave only Marvin Gardens to complete the set.

A counter asking for Atlantic Avenue plus cash is unlikely to succeed. Baltic Avenue is nearly worthless, and p4 would reject it. I cannot complete a set through this trade because p4 does not own States, Virginia, or Mediterranean.

I considered offering $350 for Atlantic Avenue. That would leave me with only about $300 cash, which is too little to buy Marvin Gardens and still pay the $600 Boardwalk rent. I rejected the idea.

Mortgaging all four properties would raise about $360, which could cover a $600 Boardwalk hit. That is too risky. p2 cannot build more houses on the dark blues without cash, so leaving them alone is correct.

Rejecting the trade is the cleanest path. I will not negotiate away Ventnor for a swap of equivalent yellows. A counter asking for a single railroad would be useless, since p1 already holds Short Line and the other rails are unowned. I will decline the offer and call out the math in my public message, staying firm without being hostile.

I am now considering an aggressive counter: offer cash for Atlantic Avenue. This would give me two yellows and block p4 from completing their yellow set. The downside is that spending cash reduces my ability to survive the $600 Boardwalk rent.

A counter asking for Atlantic Avenue would waste a negotiation turn if p4 rejects it, since the scenario allows only twenty exchanges. They value yellows highly and will not sell Atlantic cheaply, so the offer is unlikely to succeed.

I rejected the counter. A fair price for Atlantic Avenue would drain my survival cash. I will not signal desperation by offering to buy it. I will keep my cash cushion and continue blocking p1's orange and p4's light blue sets.
